references.text: The laws regarding exemption from war include the one who has betrothed a woman but not yet taken her as wife, as well as the one who has built a new house but not dedicated it, and the one who has planted a vineyard but not harvested its fruit—the same three situations mentioned as curses in 28:30.
Jeremiah prophesies that the enemy will take the Israelites' houses and vineyards, reflecting the curse of building a house without living in it and planting a vineyard without enjoying its fruit.
Amos warns that the people will build houses of cut stone but not live in them, and plant beautiful vineyards but not drink their wine—a direct parallel to the curse.
Zephaniah prophesies that the people's wealth will become plunder, and that they will build houses but not live in them, plant vineyards but not drink the wine—the same covenant curse.
Micah describes similar curses: sowing but not reaping, treading olives but not anointing oneself with oil, and treading grapes but not drinking wine.
Job mentions the curse that his wife will grind grain for another and other men will lie with her, reflecting the curse that another man will lie with one's betrothed.
